title: Kaplansky's quasitrace problem
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's counterexample (2026) to Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture: a separable unital C*-algebra that has normalized 2-quasitraces, and two positive contractions on which every such quasitrace fails additivity by at least 1/144. The proof is given in full from two named hypotheses: the existence theorem for quasitraces of Cuntz, Blackadar and Handelman, used only for the existence of a quasitrace, and standard facts on smooth manifolds and bundles, used for a dimension count. The first lesson defines quasitraces, proves the defect from two relations between finitely many elements, and reduces the theorem to the construction of an algebra. The second lesson proves an incidence lemma for generic bundle maps and a continuous normalization by a determinant potential. The third lesson builds bundles over products of projective spaces, with maps between successive levels that double dimensions and with a Chern class obstruction. The fourth lesson assembles weighted shifts into the algebra and proves that no matrix algebra over it is properly infinite. It also shows that seven generators and any bound above 1/2 suffice, so that every constant below 1/28 occurs.
prerequisites: course Foundations of von Neumann algebras, lesson Order, local units and quotients of C*-algebras: C*-algebras, positivity, the continuous functional calculus, spectral permanence, generated C*-subalgebras

course Characteristic classes, lessons Chern classes and the integral universal ring (definition (1.2), Proposition 1.1, Theorem 2.2) and The Gysin sequence and projective splitting (Theorems 3.2 and 4.1)
linear algebra (core course Linear Algebra), Lebesgue measure on R^n, compactness
the lessons prove every other fact they use, except the named hypotheses (CBH) of the first lesson and (SM) of the second lesson and the quoted consequences in Section 6 of the first lesson

Differences of presentation, none a correction: the tautological line bundle is used in place of the hyperplane bundle, which changes the top Chern class by the sign (-1)^p; the cohomology of a product of projective spaces is derived from the projective-bundle module theorem of the programme in place of the Kuenneth formula; the min-max principle, the determinant expansion, the polar part and the orthogonal complement of a subbundle are proved; continuity of the minimizer is proved with nets, for general compact Hausdorff bases. Observations added, each with its proof: seven maps can replace the sixteen and eight maps (both incidence conditions hold with q = 7, and the two lists can be merged because a subspace is at least as large as each of its projections; six maps fail the dimension count over a point); the normalization works with any coefficient theta in (0, 2), which gives any bound c > 1/2; together these give the additivity defect (1 - c)/14 for every c in (1/2, 1), so every constant below 1/28 occurs, against 1/144. open_obligations: Named hypothesis (CBH): a unital C*-algebra none of whose matrix algebras is properly infinite has a normalized 2-quasitrace (Cuntz; Blackadar and Handelman; in the form of Milhoj and Rordam, arXiv:2309.17412, Theorem 2.3). It is not proved in the programme. Only the existence of a quasitrace on the algebra A depends on it; the defect inequality for all normalized 1-quasitraces and the absence of tracial states do not.

Named hypothesis (SM): standard facts on smooth manifolds and smooth vector bundles (finitely many local frames and a smooth partition of unity; the bundle of pairs of subspaces is a compact smooth manifold of the stated dimension; kernels of fiberwise surjective smooth bundle maps are smooth bundles; a smooth manifold is a countable union of compact subsets of chart domains, on which smooth maps are Lipschitz). It is not proved in this course and was not checked against the core course on smooth manifolds. It is used only in the incidence lemma, on which the construction depends.

The consequences in Section 6 of the first lesson (the equivalence with Kaplansky's question on AW*-factors, Haagerup's theorem for exact algebras, the tensor product with the reduced C*-algebra of the free group, a stably finite algebra without tracial state) are quoted from the manuscript and the literature named there; they are not proved in the programme, and the cited theorems were not checked.

The programme results on C*-algebras and Chern classes that are used are cited with their numbers; their proofs were not checked again for this course. The characteristic classes course is by another author of the programme (GPT-6.1 Sol).
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
